The roadside roster

Guides from two settlements have brought a roster of scattered households, totaling 480 people. Native humans and mutants, children and elders alike, are hoping for a place to settle with beds, medical care, and a school.

Registering the roster only establishes contact. Large-scale admission requires convoys, travel rations, medicine, and tools, with enough food set aside for new arrivals. If convoys are paused, individual travelers who show up can still be admitted from the roster.
Register Households and Admission Terms

All registered residents receive the same food rations, medical care, and school access for children. Convoys will bring people in batches, depending on available housing and food and medicine stocks.
The Town's Public Responsibilities
With 80 residents, a clinic, classrooms, and roads for travel, the town has been running steadily. Neighbors support formally establishing housing, provisions, and public accounts as town governance.
Establishing town governance will not create extra workers or supplies. Future expansion of neighborhoods and work zones will still depend on research, construction, and everyone's hard work.
Formal town governance has been entered into the public record. The workshop can begin researching town projects.
Provisions are fluctuating. Revisit town governance once things are stable again.
Core Town Service Handover
With 400 residents and provisions, schools, and public works running steadily, the town has the foundation to connect surrounding districts.

Registration alone will not add residents to Old Town. Next, connect nearby settlements on the “City Region” page. Once at least two districts are connected, the population reaches 10,000, and public services are stable, the town can be formally registered as a city of 10,000.
Register Core Town Public Responsibilities
The core town has completed its public service handover. Continue surveying nearby areas, building roads, and sharing responsibility for the districts on the “City Region” page.
Stabilize the core town's daily provisions first.
The First City

With 400 residents who have made their homes here, irrigation channels, clinics, and classrooms running day and night, rows of cooperative housing, and projects built with neighbors, the foundations of a city are finally in place.

With 400 residents who have made their homes here, farms, clinics, classrooms, work zones, and the power grid running day and night, a city has finally taken shape. The public projects promised to neighbors have also been delivered.
But the people in the city still need to eat tomorrow. Settlements beyond the walls still govern themselves, and this land is still far from a true urban cluster.
Register the City and Its Public Responsibilities
The people have registered the home they built with their own hands as “Hearth City.” Its homes, fields, work zones, and responsibilities will be left to those who come after.
Provisions are fluctuating. Revisit establishing the city once things are stable again.
